Explain why consistent member identifiers matter in a library’s loan database

markscheme.marking_summary: Each loan’s member reference must correspond to the intended member record. Inconsistent identifiers can disconnect or misattribute loans,so staff cannot trust who owes an item. Enforced foreign-key and update rules preserve the relationship.

mappings.scope_evidence:

• Benefits of databases: community support, concurrency control, data consistency, data integrity, data retrieval, reduced data duplication, reduced redundancy, reliable transaction processing, scalability, security features
• Limitations of databases: “big data” scalability issues, design complexity, hierarchical data handling, rigid schema, object-relational impedance mismatch, unstructured data handling
mappings.rationale: Explain why consistent member identifiers matter in a library’s loan database assesses Explain the features, benefits and limitations of a relational database.

practice_questions.question_text: Explain why consistent member identifiers matter in a library’s loan database.
practice_questions.adaptation_rationale: Rebuilt scenario and response wording while retaining the supported reasoning; source-specific obsolete material excluded.
practice_questions.solution: Each loan’s member reference must correspond to the intended member record. Inconsistent identifiers can disconnect or misattribute loans,so staff cannot trust who owes an item. Enforced foreign-key and update rules preserve the relationship.

practice_questions.question_text: Describe how two restricted read-only views could let tutors and finance staff see different data from the same underlying student database.
practice_questions.adaptation_rationale: Rebuilt scenario and response wording while retaining the supported reasoning; source-specific obsolete material excluded.

practice_questions.question_text: A flat relation has StudentID,StudentName,MajorID,MajorName,CourseID,CourseName. A student has one major and many courses; a course has many students. StudentID determines StudentName and MajorID; MajorID determines MajorName; CourseID determines CourseName. Construct a3NF schema with primary keys and foreign keys.
practice_questions.adaptation_rationale: Rebuilt scenario and response wording while retaining the supported reasoning; source-specific obsolete material excluded.
practice_questions.solution: STUDENT(StudentID PK,StudentName,MajorID FK); MAJOR(MajorID PK,MajorName); COURSE(CourseID PK,CourseName); ENROLMENT(StudentID PK/FK,CourseID PK/FK). ENROLMENT has a composite key.

marking_points.criterion: Correct ENROLMENT with both foreign keys.
Correct composite enrolment key; no transitive major-name dependency.

practice_questions.question_text: Explain how modelling entities,attributes,keys and relationships before implementing a database helps it support its intended use.
practice_questions.adaptation_rationale: Rebuilt scenario and response wording while retaining the supported reasoning; source-specific obsolete material excluded.
practice_questions.solution: The model identifies what must be stored and which records relate. Suitable keys uniquely identify records and connect tables; cardinalities prevent incorrect relationship assumptions. Reviewing the model can expose omissions or redundancy before they become implementation problems.
